questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a sub-atomic particle?
questions.corrige_markdown: The three sub-atomic particles of an atom are the proton, the neutron and the electron. "Nucleon" is only a collective name for a particle found in the nucleus (a proton or a neutron); it is not a separate kind of particle. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following relights a glowing splint?
questions.corrige_markdown: Oxygen supports combustion, so it relights a glowing splint: this is the standard test for oxygen. Carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide put a flame out, and nitrogen dioxide (a brown gas) is not the test gas. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is ammonia described as an alkaline gas?
questions.corrige_markdown: A gas is called alkaline because it dissolves in the moisture on damp litmus paper to form a basic solution, $\mathrm{NH_3 + H_2O \rightleftharpoons NH_4^+ + OH^-}$, which turns red litmus blue. White fumes with concentrated hydrochloric acid ($\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$) are a test for ammonia, not the reason it is alkaline. Ammonia, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, itself contains no hydroxide ion; the $\mathrm{OH^-}$ ions only form after it dissolves in water. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: It turns damped red Litmus paper blue
It forms white fumes with conc. $\mathrm{HCl_{(aq)}}$
It has no effect on litmus paper

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a fertilizer made from Sulphuric acid
questions.corrige_markdown: Ammonia neutralises sulphuric acid: $2\mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow (\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}$. Ammonium sulphate supplies nitrogen to crops. Ammonium nitrate is made from nitric acid, potassium chloride is not made from sulphuric acid, and ammonium sulphite would come from sulphurous acid. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following substances causes hardness in water?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hardness is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium ions, which stop soap from lathering. Only $\mathrm{MgSO_4}$ contains such an ion ($\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$; it gives permanent hardness). Sodium and potassium salts do not make water hard (sodium carbonate is in fact a water softener). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the number of neutrons in the atom with a mass number of 35 and an atomic number of 17.
questions.corrige_markdown: Number of neutrons = mass number - atomic number = $35 - 17 = 18$. The trap is to add (52) or to quote the proton number (17). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the function of Chlorine in the treatment of water?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorine is added at the end of water treatment as a disinfectant: it kills disease-causing germs (bacteria). Solid particles are removed earlier by sedimentation, coagulation and filtration. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 8-9

A current of 1.5 A is passed for 1hour 30minutes during the purification of copper by electrolysis.

Which of the following reactions takes place at the anode?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the purification of copper the impure copper is the anode. Oxidation takes place at the anode: copper atoms lose electrons and go into solution, $\mathrm{Cu_{(s)} \rightarrow Cu^{2+} + 2e^-}$. The reverse reaction (B) is the one at the cathode, where pure copper is deposited. Options C and D are not valid half-equations. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 8-9

A current of 1.5 A is passed for 1hour 30minutes during the purification of copper by electrolysis.

Calculate the mass of pure copper deposited at the Anode?
questions.corrige_markdown: Charge: $Q = It = 1.5 \times (90 \times 60) = 8100\ \mathrm{C}$. Copper needs 2 faradays per mole: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2\mathrm{e^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$. Moles of $\mathrm{Cu} = \dfrac{8100}{2 \times 96\,500} = 0.042$ mol. Mass $= 0.042 \times 64 = 2.69\ \mathrm{g} \approx 2.70\ \mathrm{g}$ (exactly $2.70$ g with $1\ \mathrm{F} = 96\,000\ \mathrm{C}$). The other options come from forgetting to convert 1 h 30 min to seconds or forgetting the factor 2. Note: as printed the question says \"at the anode\", but the pure copper is deposited at the cathode (the anode dissolves); the intended quantity is the mass of copper deposited. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the equation

$2\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{Na_2CO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{X} + \mathrm{CO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

Identify the organic compound, X.
questions.corrige_markdown: Ethanoic acid reacts with a carbonate to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water. Balancing the equation: $2\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{Na_2CO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CH_3COONa} + \mathrm{CO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ (C: 5 = 5, H: 8 = 8, O: 7 = 7, Na: 2 = 2). So X is $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$, sodium ethanoate (the salt of a two-carbon acid, not methanoate which has one carbon). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two elements M and P have atomic number 12 and 7 respectively. Give the formula of the compound formed between M and P
questions.corrige_markdown: M (atomic number 12) has configuration 2,8,2 and loses 2 electrons to form $\mathrm{M^{2+}}$. P (atomic number 7) has configuration 2,5 and gains 3 electrons to form $\mathrm{P^{3-}}$. To balance charges we need 3 ions of M ($+6$) and 2 ions of P ($-6$): $\mathrm{M_3P_2}$. The trap is to write $\mathrm{M_2P_3}$ by taking the valencies in the wrong order. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A soil sample has a pH of 4. The soil sample is
questions.corrige_markdown: A pH below 7 means acidic (pH 7 is neutral, pH above 7 is basic or alkaline). A pH of 4 is therefore acidic. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A hydrocarbon contains 85.7% C and 14.3% H. Determine the empirical formula of the hydrocarbon.
questions.corrige_markdown: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass: C: $85.7 \div 12 = 7.14$; H: $14.3 \div 1 = 14.3$. Divide by the smaller value: C: $1$; H: $14.3 \div 7.14 = 2.0$. The simplest whole-number ratio is $1:2$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CH_2}$. ($\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ has the same ratio but is not the simplest formula.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a few drops of aqueous silver nitrate is added to a salt solution, a yellow precipitate is formed. Identify the anion in the salt.
questions.corrige_markdown: Silver nitrate solution is used to test for halide ions: chloride gives a white precipitate (AgCl), bromide a cream precipitate (AgBr) and iodide a yellow precipitate (AgI). Silver fluoride is soluble, so there is no precipitate for fluoride. The anion is iodide. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: State the function of Super-heated water in the extraction of sulphur.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the Frasch process, water heated to about $170^\circ\mathrm{C}$ under pressure is pumped down to the underground sulphur. Sulphur melts at about $113^\circ\mathrm{C}$, so the hot water melts it. Sulphur does not dissolve in water, and the molten sulphur is then forced up by compressed air. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the equation

$\mathrm{CuO_{(s)} + H_{2(g)} \rightarrow Cu_{(s)} + H_2O_{(g)}}$

Select from the equation, the oxidizing agent.
questions.corrige_markdown: An oxidizing agent is the substance that is reduced (it gives oxygen to, or removes electrons from, the other substance). Copper(II) oxide loses oxygen and the copper goes from $+2$ to $0$, so $\mathrm{CuO}$ is reduced and is the oxidizing agent. Hydrogen gains oxygen (it is oxidised), so it is the reducing agent. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 17-18

The following diagram represents a separation technique used to separate a mixture of X and Y

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Identify a pair of substances that could be X and Y respectively.
questions.corrige_markdown: The diagram shows a separating funnel holding two layers: X is the upper layer and Y the lower layer, so the two liquids do not mix (they are immiscible) and X is less dense than Y. Petrol floats on water, so X = petrol and Y = water. Ethanol with petrol and petrol with kerosene are miscible and would not form layers. Option D has the water on top, which is the wrong way round. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 17-18

The following diagram represents a separation technique used to separate a mixture of X and Y

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

State the property of X and Y that makes it suitable for separation by this method.
questions.corrige_markdown: A separating funnel separates immiscible liquids. They settle in two layers because they have different densities (the denser liquid at the bottom), and the lower layer is then run off through the tap. Volatility, melting points and boiling points are used in distillation or crystallisation, not in a separating funnel. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Arrange the elements; Calcium, Iron, Sodium and Zinc in order of increasing reactivity, starting from the least reactive.
questions.corrige_markdown: The reactivity series (most reactive first) is: potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, lead, hydrogen, copper. Reading it from the bottom for our four metals gives iron (least reactive), then zinc, then calcium, then sodium (most reactive). A common trap is to put sodium and calcium in the wrong order or to put zinc below iron. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 20-22

**Instructions (Questions 20-22):** each of the following questions consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether each of the statements is TRUE or FALSE. Then choose A, B, C or D.

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| Alkali metals are very good reducing agents | The alkali metals are easily oxidized |
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. An alkali metal has one electron in its outer shell which it loses very easily, $\mathrm{M \rightarrow M^+ + e^-}$, so it is easily oxidized. A substance that is easily oxidized gives electrons readily to other species, which is exactly what a reducing agent does. So the second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: If both statements are true and the second statement is a correct explanation of the first statement
If both statements are true but the second statement is not a correct explanation of the first statement
If the first statement is true but the second statement is false
If the first statement is false but the second statement is true

Questions 20-22

**Instructions (Questions 20-22):** each of the following questions consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Decide whether each of the statements is TRUE or FALSE. Then choose A, B, C or D.

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| $\mathrm{C_2H_2}$ and $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$ have the same chemical and physical properties | $\mathrm{C_2H_2}$ and $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$ have the same percentage by mass of hydrogen |
questions.corrige_markdown: First statement: ethyne ($\mathrm{C_2H_2}$, a gas) and benzene ($\mathrm{C_6H_6}$, a liquid) are different compounds with different physical and chemical properties, so it is false. Second statement: both have the empirical formula $\mathrm{CH}$, so the percentage of hydrogen by mass is the same: $\dfrac{2 \times 1}{26} = \dfrac{6 \times 1}{78} = 7.7\%$. It is true. The first statement is false and the second is true. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: If both statements are true and the second statement is a correct explanation of the first statement
If both statements are true but the second statement is not a correct explanation of the first statement
If the first statement is true but the second statement is false
If the first statement is false but the second statement is true

| First statement | Second statement |

questions.corrige_markdown: First statement: indicators such as litmus and methyl orange are dyes, so it is true. Second statement: an indicator changes colour with any acid or base, including weak ones (litmus turns red in ethanoic acid, a weak acid), so it is false. The first is true and the second is false. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following carbonates is stable on heating?
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbonates of the more reactive metals are more stable to heat. Sodium carbonate does not decompose at ordinary Bunsen temperatures. Lithium carbonate (the least stable of Group I), calcium carbonate ($\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}$) and ammonium carbonate (which breaks down easily) all decompose on heating. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following will decolourise bromine water?
questions.corrige_markdown: Bromine water is decolourised (orange to colourless) by unsaturated compounds because bromine adds across the double bond: $\mathrm{C_2H_4 + Br_2 \rightarrow C_2H_4Br_2}$. Ethene is the only unsaturated compound in the list; ethane and butane are saturated alkanes and ethanol is an alcohol. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 25-26

Consider the energy level diagram below for a reversible reaction:

![fig-2](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

What heat change occurs in the reaction?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the diagram the products ($2\mathrm{NH_{3(g)}}$) are at a lower energy level than the reactants ($\mathrm{N_{2(g)} + 3H_{2(g)}}$), and $\Delta H$ points downwards. Energy is given out to the surroundings, so the reaction is exothermic and heat is released. Options A and B describe an endothermic reaction. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Heat is absorbed during the reaction

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 25-26

Consider the energy level diagram below for a reversible reaction:

![fig-2](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

What is the effect of an increase in pressure on the equilibrium position?
questions.corrige_markdown: The reaction is $\mathrm{N_2 + 3H_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3}$: 4 moles of gas on the left and 2 moles on the right. By Le Chatelier's principle, a higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules, so the equilibrium shifts to the right (more ammonia). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Equilibrium position shifts both to the right and left

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the percentage composition of oxygen in air
questions.corrige_markdown: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.03% carbon dioxide and about 1% noble gases. Oxygen is 21%. The trap is 78% (nitrogen) or 1% (argon and other noble gases). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the percentage composition by mass of Nitrogen in Ammonium phosphate $(\mathrm{NH_4})_3\mathrm{PO_4}$. (RMM = 149)
questions.corrige_markdown: There are 3 nitrogen atoms in the formula, so the mass of nitrogen is $3 \times 14 = 42$. Percentage of N $= \dfrac{42}{149} \times 100 = 28.2\%$. Option B ($9.4\%$) is $14/149$, which counts only one N atom, and option D ($20.8\%$) is $31/149$, the percentage of phosphorus. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 29-31

**Instructions (Questions 29-31):** for each of the questions, ONE or MORE of the response(s) given is (are) correct. Decide which of the response(s) is (are) correct. Then choose: A. If 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B. If 1 and 3 are correct; C. If 2 and 4 are correct; D. If 4 only is correct.

Which of the following substances is(are) allotropic?

1. Carbon
2. Sulphur
3. Phosphorus
4. Calcium Carbonate
questions.corrige_markdown: Allotropes are different physical forms of the same element in the same state. Carbon (diamond, graphite), sulphur (rhombic, monoclinic) and phosphorus (red, white) are all allotropic. Calcium carbonate is a compound, so it cannot have allotropes. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 29-31

**Instructions (Questions 29-31):** for each of the questions, ONE or MORE of the response(s) given is (are) correct. Decide which of the response(s) is (are) correct. Then choose: A. If 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B. If 1 and 3 are correct; C. If 2 and 4 are correct; D. If 4 only is correct.

Transition metals have the following characteristic properties:

1. Form coloured compounds
2. Are malleable and ductile
3. Have variable oxidation states
4. Conduct electricity

*Options as printed:* A) 1, 2 and 3 only   B) 1 and 3 only   C) 2 and 4 only   D) 4 only
questions.corrige_markdown:
The properties that are *characteristic* of transition metals, that is, the ones that set them apart from other metals such as Group I and II, are that they form coloured compounds (1) and show variable oxidation states (3); they are also good catalysts. Being malleable and ductile (2) and conducting electricity (4) are properties of all metals, so they do not characterise transition metals in particular. Statements 1 and 3 are therefore selected. Note: strictly speaking all four statements are true of transition metals; the answer expected by the examiners is the one that keeps only the distinguishing properties. **Most likely expected answer: B (1 and 3 only).**

This question is left open for self-assessment: its answer key is debatable (see the remark above), so it is not auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 29-31

**Instructions (Questions 29-31):** for each of the questions, ONE or MORE of the response(s) given is (are) correct. Decide which of the response(s) is (are) correct. Then choose: A. If 1, 2 and 3 are correct; B. If 1 and 3 are correct; C. If 2 and 4 are correct; D. If 4 only is correct.

Substance X reacts with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ producing copper(II)sulphate salt. Identify X

1. Copper metal
2. Copper oxide
3. Copper hydroxide
4. Copper carbonate

*Options as printed:* A) 1, 2 and 3 only B) 1 and 3 only C) 2 and 4 only D) 4 only
questions.corrige_markdown: Copper metal is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not react with dilute sulphuric acid (1 is wrong). The other three do give copper(II) sulphate: $\mathrm{CuO + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 + H_2O}$; $\mathrm{Cu(OH)_2 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 + 2H_2O}$; $\mathrm{CuCO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 + H_2O + CO_2}$. **The correct set is statements 2, 3 and 4.** None of the printed options A to D gives this set (C, the nearest, omits 3), so the question is faulty as printed and has no valid letter.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Why does powdering marble chips increase the rate of the following reaction;

$\mathrm{CaCO_{3(s)} + 2HCl_{(aq)} \rightarrow CaCl_{2(aq)} + CO_{2(g)} + H_2O_{(l)}}$
questions.corrige_markdown: Powdering breaks the marble into many small pieces, so the total surface area exposed to the acid increases (not reduces). More particles of marble are in contact with the acid, so the acid particles collide with them more often: the collision frequency increases, and the reaction is faster. Options A, C and D each say the opposite of what happens. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The number of effective collision decreases
The rate increases with less contact of marble and acid

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a reduction reaction?
questions.corrige_markdown: Reduction is gain of electrons (OIL RIG). In A, B and C electrons appear on the right-hand side, so electrons are lost: they are oxidations. In D, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ gains 2 electrons to become copper metal, so D is the reduction. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How is chlorine collected in the laboratory?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorine is about 2.5 times denser than air, so it sinks and is collected in a gas jar by downward delivery (the gas displaces the air upwards out of the jar). It is not collected over water because it dissolves in water (and reacts with it). Upward delivery and downward displacement of air are for gases lighter than air such as ammonia. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $0.1\ \mathrm{M}\ \mathrm{NaOH}$ neutralizes $20\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ solution. Calculate the concentration of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
questions.corrige_markdown: Equation: $2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$. Moles of NaOH $= 0.1 \times \dfrac{25}{1000} = 0.0025$ mol. The mole ratio $\mathrm{NaOH} : \mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is $2:1$, so moles of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = 0.00125$ mol. Concentration $= \dfrac{0.00125}{0.020} = 0.0625\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$. The trap is to forget the $2:1$ ratio, which gives $0.125$ M (option A). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the oxidizing agent from the equation;

$2\mathrm{H_2S_{(g)} + SO_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2H_2O_{(l)} + 3S_{(s)}}$
questions.corrige_markdown: Sulphur is $-2$ in $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $+4$ in $\mathrm{SO_2}$ and $0$ in the product $\mathrm{S}$. $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is reduced ($+4 \rightarrow 0$), so it is the oxidizing agent; $\mathrm{H_2S}$ is oxidised ($-2 \rightarrow 0$) and is the reducing agent. The equation is balanced (S: 3 = 3, H: 4 = 4, O: 2 = 2). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mixture is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A mixture contains two or more substances that are only physically mixed (not chemically combined), so they keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods. B describes a compound, C describes an element and D describes matter in general. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: A substance that contains two or more substances not chemically combined
A substance formed when two or more substances combine chemically through bond formation.
A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler units
A substance that has weight and occupies space.

questions.enonce_markdown: Elements A and B have atomic numbers 12 and 16 respectively. Identify the type of bonding formed between them
questions.corrige_markdown: A (atomic number 12) is 2,8,2, a metal that loses 2 electrons to form $\mathrm{A^{2+}}$. B (atomic number 16) is 2,8,6, a non-metal that gains 2 electrons to form $\mathrm{B^{2-}}$. Transfer of electrons between a metal and a non-metal gives ionic bonding (compound $\mathrm{AB}$, i.e. MgS). (Options A and C are printed identically.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: From the electronic configurations, which of the following belong to the same period?
questions.corrige_markdown: The number of occupied shells gives the period. A: 4 shells and 3 shells (periods 4 and 3). B: 2 shells and 3 shells (periods 2 and 3). C: 3 shells and 3 shells, both in period 3 (sodium and aluminium). D: 3 shells and 4 shells (periods 3 and 4). Only C has the same number of shells. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 40-41 concern the following diagram:

![fig-3](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

Identify the gas, A, that can be dried and collected in this way.
questions.corrige_markdown: The gas is dried in a U-tube containing a solid drying agent and is then collected in a gas jar held upside down, with the delivery tube reaching to the top of the jar (upward delivery, also called downward displacement of air). This method is used for a gas that is less dense than air and is alkaline: ammonia. $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ and $\mathrm{SO_2}$ are denser than air and acidic, so they are collected by downward delivery. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 40-41 concern the following diagram:

![fig-3](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

Identify the drying agent 'B'
questions.corrige_markdown: Ammonia is alkaline, so it can only be dried with a basic drying agent. Quicklime (calcium oxide, a solid, suitable for a U-tube) does not react with ammonia. Calcium chloride combines with ammonia, and concentrated sulphuric acid (also a liquid, so not used in a U-tube) reacts to form ammonium sulphate. Slaked lime is not used as a drying agent. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following chemical equations is balanced?
questions.corrige_markdown: Count the atoms on each side. A: H is 1 on the left and 2 on the right, Cl is 1 and 2; it needs $2\mathrm{HCl}$. B (as printed): H is 8 on the left and 2 on the right. C: O is 3 on the left and 2 on the right; it needs $2\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO_2}$. D: Mg 1 = 1, H 2 = 2, N 2 = 2, O 6 = 6, so it is balanced. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A salt which when exposed to air forms a solution is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A deliquescent substance absorbs so much water vapour from the air that it dissolves in it and forms a solution (e.g. sodium hydroxide, calcium chloride). An efflorescent salt loses water of crystallisation to the air. A hygroscopic substance only absorbs water without necessarily dissolving. A hydrated salt simply contains water of crystallisation. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 44-45

The diagram shows the rate of a reaction at different concentrations.

![fig-4](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Which of the curves shows the fastest reaction rate?
questions.corrige_markdown: The rate of reaction is the gradient of the curve of volume against time. W is the steepest curve and reaches the plateau first, so it is the fastest. Z has the smallest gradient and is the slowest. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 44-45

The diagram shows the rate of a reaction at different concentrations.

![fig-4](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Which of the curves corresponds to the reaction with reactants having the lowest concentration?
questions.corrige_markdown: A lower concentration means fewer particles per unit volume, fewer collisions per second and therefore a slower reaction. The slowest reaction is the one with the smallest gradient, Z, and it is the last to reach the plateau. All the curves level off at the same final volume, so only the speed differs. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the product formed when hexan-1,6-diamine reacts with hexanedioic acid
questions.corrige_markdown: Hexane-1,6-diamine (an amine with two $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ groups) and hexanedioic acid (a dicarboxylic acid) join by condensation polymerisation, losing water at each link to form amide ($\mathrm{-CONH-}$) links. The polyamide formed is nylon-6,6 (6 carbons in each monomer). Terylene is a polyester, Perspex is poly(methyl 2-methylpropenoate) and styrene is a monomer. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which gas is always given off when a metal nitrate is heated?
questions.corrige_markdown: Every metal nitrate gives off oxygen when heated. Nitrates of potassium and sodium give the nitrite and oxygen only ($2\mathrm{NaNO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaNO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$), while most other metal nitrates also give brown nitrogen dioxide ($2\mathrm{Cu(NO_3)_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CuO} + 4\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}$). So only oxygen is given off in every case. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A current of 2A was passed for 90 minutes through an electrolytic cell. Calculate the quantity of electricity in coulombs.
questions.corrige_markdown: $Q = It$ with $t$ in seconds: $t = 90 \times 60 = 5400\ \mathrm{s}$, so $Q = 2 \times 5400 = 10\,800\ \mathrm{C}$. The trap is to use minutes directly ($2 \times 90 = 180$, option A). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the charge on a proton?
questions.corrige_markdown: A proton carries a charge of $+1$ (positive). The electron is negative and the neutron has no charge. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The change of state from solid to liquid is known as
questions.corrige_markdown: Solid to liquid is melting. Condensation is gas to liquid, freezing is liquid to solid and sublimation is solid to gas directly. **Answer: B.**
